column1: # npm-pre-scan evaluation corpus — BROAD LEGITIMATE CONTROL (top-downloads)
# Purpose : a false-positive control for the 399 purpose-built `malicious_intent` packages
#           in datadog_intent.tsv, which have no legitimate twin. Every flag raised here is
# Source  : the first 500 names of data/top_packages.txt (curated top-downloads snapshot),
#           with any package appearing in the DataDog malicious corpora removed
# Layers  : 1 only, to match how datadog_intent.tsv is scored.
# ⚠ READ THE BIAS BEFORE QUOTING ANY FIGURE FROM THIS FILE. These are popular,
#   well-maintained packages; the malicious half is tiny, obscure and freshly published.
#   The two populations differ in every respect except being npm packages, so precision
#   measured across them is OPTIMISTIC — it says "the tool does not cry wolf on what people
#   actually install", NOT "the tool separates malicious from legitimate packages of similar
#   shape". The matched arm (datadog_clean.tsv) is what answers the second question.
